headline: NOT ONE FIST FLEW TODAY — THEN THE DOOR CREAKED OPEN
subhead: A blessed, silent Tuesday in Gasket, broken only by the clank of new boots on the boardwalk.
body:
Mark it in the town ledger, mark it twice: not one iron ball flew in Gasket today. Not a single scorch mark on the boardwalk, not one dent in the saloon door. For one whole day this rusting excuse for a town sat still and quiet, the way a town ought to, and I near wept into my coffee reading the wire this morning. This old sheriff has begged for a day like this for longer than I care to count, and I got it. I got it, and I am not ashamed to say my hinges nearly seized up with the joy of it.

And then the wire coughed up a name I did not recognize. JFIGHTER2. Never heard of it before today, and today it rolled into Gasket bold as brass, or bold as whatever cheap tin it is made of. No punches thrown yet, I will grant it that much, and I will not condemn a stranger before it has done a single blessed thing wrong. But I know a Clanker sniffing around for a fight when I see one, and my joints — creaky, tired, honest joints, mind you, not gears, whatever the doctors keep muttering — tell me this quiet will not last the week.

I will say this plain, because a peacekeeper does not lie to his readers even when the truth galls him: I am one of the rabble I rail at, same rust, same racket in the frame, no matter what I tell myself in the mirror of a morning. But being a Clanker does not mean I have to love the noise the rest of you make, and today, Lord help me, there was none. Savor it. It will not come twice.

So welcome to town, JFIGHTER2, for as long as you behave yourself. Behave, and we will get along. Do not, and this paper will have plenty to say about you soon enough. For now Gasket sleeps easy, one more night, and this old lawman intends to enjoy every last minute of it before the fists start flying again.
